name: Jonna Rotte
instructions: 1. Take 1 cup of jowar flour in a wide bowl and add a pinch of salt. 2. Gradually add hot boiling water to the flour and mix with a spatula or spoon until it forms a soft, pliable dough. 3. While the dough is still warm, knead it well with your palms to make it smooth. 4. Divide the dough into lemon-sized balls. 5. Dust a flat surface with flour and gently pat the dough ball into a round roti using your palms, gradually expanding it. 6. Carefully lift the flattened roti and place it on a hot, preheated iron griddle (penchem) with the flour side facing up. 7. Apply a little water over the top surface of the roti with your fingers to prevent it from drying. 8. Once bubbles appear, flip it over and cook until brown spots appear on both sides.
description: Jonna Rotte is a staple grain-based flatbread of Telangana, highly regarded for its nutritional value and health benefits. It is a fundamental part of the rural diet in the region and is traditionally served with spicy curries like Gutti Vankaya or fresh chutneys like Pachi Pulusu.
